name: Manipuri
world_status: accessible description is silent on stress

earlier_scan.source_named: Chelliah, Shobhana L. 1997. A Grammar of Meithei. Mouton de Gruyter (phonology chapter); paywalled, no open copy found. Also Abbi & Mishra 1993 Some aspects of Meitei phonology.

new_statements.quote: The supra-segmental phonemes in Meitei are two tones. Length is not phonemic in this language.
new_statements.citation: Abbi, Anvita & Awadhesh K. Mishra. [1987]. Some Aspects of Meitei Phonology. 24 pp. ERIC document ED286374 (FL 016 924), section 1.2 'Supra-Segmental Phonemes'.
new_statements.locator: sec. 1.2, p. 4 (PDF page 4 of the ERIC microfiche scan)
new_statements.rule_in_words: Meithei is described by every accessible source as a lexical tone language with a two-way root tone contrast (high vs low; Bhat & Ningomba call it high-falling vs level; Inder Singh 1975 distinguishes three phonetic tones falling/rising/level); tone is a property of roots/syllables, affixes are toneless and take their pitch from the root (Chelliah 2003: 428). No accessible description states where word stress falls or whether stress exists as a separate prominence: Abbi & Mishra list tones as the only suprasegmental phonemes; Inder Singh 1975 (p. 15) names 'Tones, Stress and Intonation' as the suprasegmental categories but describes only tones; Chelliah 1990, 1997 (pp. 17-21), 2003 and Bhat & Ningomba 1997 never mention stress.
new_statements.exceptions: None. Companion statement, Singh, Inder 1975. Manipuri Phonetic Reader, p. 15: 'Suprasegmental sounds can be further classified into Tones Stress and Intonation. Tones are the only suprasegmentals which are discussed in this Reader. The domain of Tones are syllables in Manipuri.' Chelliah 1990: 98-99 notes that L2 vs L3 compounds 'may... differ with regard to suprasegmental features. Further research will have to be conducted'.
new_statements.domain_note: Word/root level: tone is lexically specified on roots (monosyllabic in native vocabulary) and spreads over affixed words by upstep/downstep (Chelliah 2003). Descriptions are of the Imphal standard dialect (Chelliah 2003: 427); Abbi & Mishra's data are from c. 40 speakers in Imphal. No source discusses citation-form vs phrase prominence.
new_statements.identity_note: All sources describe standard (Imphal) Meithei = mani1292; Singh 1989 additionally describes the Kwatha village dialect (no separate glottocode known). Inder Singh 1975 analyses three tones (falling, rising, level) where Chelliah and Bhat & Ningomba analyse two; this is an analytic difference, not a variety difference. Bishnupriya Manipuri (Indo-Aryan) is a different language and was excluded.

Tones are the only suprasegmentals which are discussed in this Reader. The domain of Tones are syllables in Manipuri.' Describes three tones (falling, rising, level; pp. 15-19, 62-63, 73-74); stress is named as a category but never described.

sources.citation: WALS Online, language Meithei (wals_code mei), checked against cldf-datasets/wals.
sources.note: Meithei has no datapoints in the stress chapters 14A-17A (Goedemans & van der Hulst), so WALS/StressTyp carry no stress value for it. StressTyp2 site (StressTyp2.ullet.net) was unreachable.

sources.citation: Chelliah, Shobhana L. 2003. Meithei. In Graham Thurgood & Randy J. LaPolla (eds.), The Sino-Tibetan Languages, 427-438. London: Routledge.
sources.note: Sec. 2.1 Syllable structure and 2.2 Tone (p. 428): 'Meithei exhibits a two-way contrast on roots between low and high tone. Suffixes and prefixes have no tone associated with them; instead, the pitch values observed for these are derived through the spreading of lexically specified root tones through the rules of downstepping and upstepping.' No mention of stress anywhere in the phonology section. Describes the Imphal (standard) dialect (p. 427).

sources.citation: Chelliah, Shobhana L. 1990. Level-ordered morphology and phonology in Manipuri. Linguistics of the Tibeto-Burman Area 13(2): 27-72. DOI 10.15144/LTBA-13.2.27.
sources.note: Segmental phoneme inventory, feature matrices, lexical rules (voicing, deaspiration, etc.) and level ordering; no stress statement. Only prosodic remark: L2 and L3 compounds 'may... differ with regard to suprasegmental features. Further research will have to be conducted' (pp. 98-99).

sources.citation: Chelliah, Shobhana L. 1997. A Grammar of Meithei (Mouton Grammar Library 17). Berlin: Mouton de Gruyter. Chapter 2 'Phonetics and phonology', pp. 17-70. Only pp. 17-21 (secs. 2.1-2.2) available as the Rosetta Project excerpt.
sources.note: Available pages cover consonant and vowel phonemes only; p. 17 announces that the chapter describes 'syllable structure, tone, and lexical and post-lexical phonological rules'; p. 18: roots 'may be marked for high tone... unmarked roots have low tone. The details of the tone system are described in section 2.4' (not in the excerpt). No stress statement in the accessible pages; the rest of the chapter is paywalled (DOI 10.1515/9783110801118.17; De Gruyter and Google Books blocked).
